newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Telecom's Xtra does not breach Act - NZCC.
newsitem.headline: Telecom's Xtra does not breach Act - NZCC.

text.p: The anti-trust New Zealand Commerce Commission said on Thursday it found no evidence that Telecom Corp of New Zealand's internet service provider, Xtra, was breaching the Commerce Act by offering below cost access to the internet.
NZCC chairman Alan Bollard said it had completed its investigation but would continue to monitor the situation.
He said that there were numerous internet service providers and barriers to entry were low.
Rival phone company, Clear Communications, had entered the market and Australia Telstra AOT.AX planed to enter even after Telecom reduced its access prices, the commission said.

NZCC said Telecom did not appear to be using a dominant position to harm competitors and its strategy did not depend for success on driving other firms from the market, but rather on developing value-added services.
Low pricing was an encouragement for the market to expand, it said. -- Wellington newsroom 64 4 4734 746
